trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Lisbon, Portugal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely afternoon at the iconic Time Out Market, sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine including pastéis de bacalhau (codfish cakes), bifanas (pork sandwiches), local cheeses, and the famous pastel de nata custard tarts from top local chefs all under one roof.

experiences.name: Belém Historical Monuments & Pastry Trail
experiences.description: Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery and the iconic Tower of Belém, both masterpieces of Manueline architecture dating to the Age of Discovery. Afterward, stop at the original Pastéis de Belém bakery, open since 1837, to taste the world-famous custard tarts made from a secret recipe.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Metro (Linha Vermelha/Red Line) from Aeroporto station to the city center for about €1.65 using a Viva Viagem card. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour: Head to the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré (about 15–20 min by Metro or tram). Spend a leisurely afternoon sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine — try a bifana (pork sandwich), fresh seafood, and a pastel de nata. Graze through multiple stalls to experience a wide variety of local flavors without committing to one expensive sit-down meal.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront Ribeira promenade as the sun sets over the Tagus River. Then explore the narrow cobblestone streets of Cais do Sodré and Bairro Alto neighborhoods. Grab a drink at a local tasca (tavern) and listen for live Fado music drifting from nearby restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and pastry at the airport café upon landing (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Graze at Time Out Market — budget €10–15 for 2–3 small dishes and a drink
meals.dinner: A Cevicheria do Mercado or a local tasca near Cais do Sodré — try arroz de marisco (seafood rice) or grilled sardines for €8–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 24-hour or rechargeable Viva Viagem Metro card at the airport (€0.50 card + credit). Keep receipts — VAT refunds may apply for non-EU visitors. The Time Out Market is open until midnight, so no rush.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Alfama, Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood. Start at the Miradouro da Graça viewpoint for sweeping panoramic views of the city and Tagus River (free). Walk downhill through winding medieval alleyways, passing colorful azulejo-tiled buildings and local laundry strung between windows. Visit the exterior of the Sé de Lisboa (Lisbon Cathedral) — free to enter the main nave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge) — entrance is €15 but offers commanding views and rich Moorish-era history. Wander the battlements and archaeological site. Alternatively, if budget is tight, enjoy the free viewpoints surrounding the castle walls. Afterward, descend into Mouraria, Lisbon's multicultural quarter, and explore its street art and local market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Experience authentic Fado in Alfama. Many small tascas offer free Fado performances with dinner — look for restaurants on Rua de São João da Praça or Rua dos Remédios. Arrive early to secure a seat.

meals.breakfast: Café near Lisbon City Stay — galão (milky coffee) and a pastel de nata for €2–3
meals.lunch: A Tasca do Chico or similar local Alfama tasca — prato do dia (dish of the day) typically €7–10 including bread, drink, and dessert
meals.dinner: Fado tasca in Alfama with dinner included — budget €15–20 for a full meal with a complimentary Fado performance

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Alfama's cobblestone hills are steep. The neighborhood is best explored on foot. Tram 28 passes through Alfama but can be very crowded on weekends; consider walking instead.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Monuments & Pastry Trail: Take the tram (Tram 15E from Praça da Figueira) or bus to Belém (~30 min, €2 with Viva Viagem card). Begin at the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery — a breathtaking masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture. The main cloister costs €10 to enter; the church is free. Spend at least 90 minutes marveling at the ornate stone carvings and royal tombs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes along the riverfront to the iconic Tower of Belém (Torre de Belém) — another UNESCO-listed Manueline gem jutting into the Tagus River. Entry is €6. Afterward, visit the nearby Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) for great river views — exterior is free, interior is €6 if interested. Explore the Belém waterfront gardens, which are free and scenic.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon (Baixa/Chiado area). Wander through Chiado's elegant streets, browse independent bookshops like Livraria Bertrand (the world's oldest operating bookshop, free to browse), and enjoy the lively Largo do Chiado square.

meals.breakfast: The legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery — the original pastel de nata birthplace since 1837. Try 2–3 pastéis with a bica (espresso) for €3–4. Arrive early as queues form quickly.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local Belém supermarket or grab a bifana sandwich from a street kiosk near the waterfront — €4–6
meals.dinner: Taberna da Rua das Flores or similar affordable Chiado restaurant — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) style dining, budget €12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Belém is about 6 km from the city center. The Tram 15E is the most scenic and budget-friendly option. Consider a combined ticket for Jerónimos + Tower of Belém for a small saving. Sundays may see longer queues at major monuments — arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Baixa (Downtown) and Rossio neighborhoods — the historic heart of Lisbon rebuilt after the 1755 earthquake. Visit Praça do Comércio (Commerce Square) on the riverfront — free and architecturally stunning. Walk up Rua Augusta through the triumphal arch (elevator to the top costs €3 for great views). Explore the elegant Praça do Rossio with its wave-patterned mosaic pavement and baroque fountain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum) — one of Lisbon's most unique and underrated museums dedicated to Portugal's iconic azulejo tile tradition. Entry is €5 (free on the first Sunday of each month). The museum is housed in a stunning 16th-century convent. Take Bus 794 from Baixa (~20 min). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the breathtaking tile panels, including a 23-meter panoramic tile depiction of pre-earthquake Lisbon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Intendente or Mouraria for an authentic local evening away from tourist crowds. Visit the Intendente square, a revitalized neighborhood hub with local cafés and street life. Try ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur) served in a chocolate cup from a street vendor near Rossio for €1.50 — a classic Lisbon experience.

meals.breakfast: Padaria (bakery) near the hotel — fresh bread roll with butter and coffee for €2–3
meals.lunch: Cervejaria Ramiro nearby or a local cervejaria (beer hall) in Baixa — bifana or prego sandwich with a beer for €5–8
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Intendente neighborhood — try caldo verde (kale soup) and bacalhau à brás (salted cod with eggs and potatoes) for €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Azulejo Museum is closed on Mondays — if so, substitute with the free Museu de Lisboa (exterior) or the Carmo Archaeological Museum (€5) in Chiado, housed in a roofless Gothic church destroyed by the 1755 earthquake — hauntingly beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the trendy LX Factory — a repurposed 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara filled with independent shops, street art, cafés, and creative studios. It's free to enter and wander. Browse local design, vintage clothing, and artisan food stalls. On Sundays it hosts a popular market, but the complex is open and vibrant on weekdays too. Take Bus 714 or 727 from Cais do Sodré (~10 min).
day_by_day.afternoon: Final exploration of Príncipe Real neighborhood — one of Lisbon's most charming upscale-bohemian areas. Visit the Jardim do Príncipe Real (a shaded garden with a giant cedar tree — free) and browse the Saturday antique market if timing aligns. Walk to the Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara for one of the city's best free panoramic viewpoints over the Baixa and the castle. Stop at a local grocery store to pick up Portuguese souvenirs: local wine (€4–6/bottle), tinned fish (sardinhas, atum), and pastéis de nata to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Bairro Alto — Lisbon's bohemian hilltop neighborhood. Enjoy a farewell meal at a classic tasca with a bottle of house wine (vinho da casa). Toast to the trip with a final glass of ginjinha or a Porto tónico (port wine and tonic). Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: LX Factory's café — artisan coffee and fresh pastry for €3–5
meals.lunch: Cervejaria or tasca in Príncipe Real — prato do dia with soup, main, drink, and dessert for €8–11
meals.dinner: Classic Bairro Alto tasca — a full Portuguese meal (soup, grilled fish or meat, dessert, and house wine) for €12–18 per person. Try restaurante Zé da Mouraria or similar neighborhood gem.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time and plan accordingly — Lisbon Airport is 20–30 min from the city center by Metro (Red Line). Keep your Viva Viagem card loaded for the airport journey. Budget tip: a full 5-day trip including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees can be managed comfortably for €60–90/day per person if disciplined.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight and prepare for the trip ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up. Take a leisurely self-guided walk around your neighborhood to get oriented — explore nearby Praça do Comércio (Commerce Square) along the Tagus riverfront, stroll through Baixa (downtown Lisbon), and ride the iconic Elevador de Santa Justa for panoramic city views. A gentle, low-key introduction to the city after your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show: Join an early evening guided walking tour through Alfama, Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood. Wind through narrow cobblestone streets, past colorful tiled facades, miradouros (viewpoints), and centuries-old churches. Cap the night with a traditional Fado music performance — Portugal's soulful, melancholic musical heritage — at a local Fado house included in the tour.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick bite at Lisbon Airport's cafés upon arrival (pastel de nata + coffee, ~€3–5).
meals.lunch: After check-in, head to A Cevicheria or Tasca do Chico in Baixa/Chiado for a relaxed Portuguese lunch — try bacalhau (salted cod) or a prego sandwich, budget ~€12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner is included as part of the Alfama Fado Show experience. Expect traditional Portuguese dishes such as caldo verde soup, grilled fish, and local wine in a cozy Fado restaurant setting.

day_by_day.notes: Since your flight lands at 13:00, allow at least 1.5–2 hours for baggage, immigration, and the 30-minute taxi/metro ride to the hotel. Don't overpack Day 1 — jet lag or travel fatigue may set in. The Fado tour typically starts around 19:00–20:00, giving you plenty of time to settle in first. Book the Fado experience in advance as it sells out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Monuments & Pastry Trail: Head west to the historic Belém district. Begin with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture built in the 16th century to honor Vasco da Gama's voyage to India. Explore its ornate cloisters and church. Then walk to the iconic Tower of Belém (Torre de Belém), standing sentinel on the Tagus River. The Manueline stonework and riverside setting make it one of Portugal's most photographed landmarks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Belém Pastry Trail — stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery (open since 1837) for the original pastel de nata, dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar. Stroll along the Belém waterfront and visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos). In the mid-afternoon, return to central Lisbon and visit the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour: explore this iconic covered market in Cais do Sodré, sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine from top local chefs and vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Bairro Alto and Chiado neighborhoods on foot. Browse independent bookshops, vintage stores, and local boutiques. Settle in for a relaxed dinner in Chiado — one of Lisbon's most charming dining districts.

meals.breakfast: Start the day at a local pastelaria near the hotel — coffee (bica) and a croissant or tosta mista, ~€3–5. Or wait and make the famous Pastéis de Belém your morning treat.
meals.lunch: Graze through the Time Out Market Lisbon in the afternoon — budget €15–25 per person sampling multiple stalls (petiscos, fresh seafood, artisan cheeses, local wines).
meals.dinner: Dine at Taberna da Rua das Flores in Chiado — a beloved traditional tasca serving seasonal Portuguese petiscos and natural wines. Expect ~€25–35 per person. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is about 6 km west of central Lisbon — take Tram 15E from Praça da Figueira or a quick Uber (~€8–10). Arrive at Jerónimos Monastery early (opens 10:00) to beat Sunday crowds. The Tower of Belém and Monastery are closed on Mondays, so Sunday is perfect. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Belém involves a fair amount of walking along the riverfront.

day_by_day.morning: National Tile Museum & Azulejo Workshop: Visit the Museu Nacional do Azulejo, housed in a stunning 16th-century convent in the Xabregas neighborhood. Spend the morning exploring five centuries of Portuguese decorative tile art — from Moorish geometric patterns to elaborate blue-and-white Baroque panels. The museum's highlight is a 23-meter panoramic azulejo panel depicting pre-earthquake Lisbon (circa 1738). After the museum tour, participate in a hands-on azulejo painting workshop and create your own tile to take home as a unique souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mouraria & Intendente Neighborhood Food & History Walk: Discover Lisbon's multicultural heart in the Mouraria quarter — the historic Moorish district and birthplace of Fado. A guided walk reveals hidden squares, street art, local grocery shops, and the stories of the diverse communities (Portuguese, African, Asian, Brazilian) who shaped this neighborhood. Sample street food and local snacks along the way, including bifanas (pork sandwiches) and ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur).
day_by_day.evening: Wander up to the Graça or Mouraria viewpoints (miradouros) for golden-hour sunset views over the city's terracotta rooftops and the Tagus River. Then enjoy a quiet dinner in the Intendente or Mouraria area at one of the neighborhood's authentic local restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Café com leite and pastéis at a neighborhood café near the hotel, ~€3–5.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Tile Museum's café or grab a bifana and ginjinha during the Mouraria food walk (snacks included in the tour experience).
meals.dinner: Try Zé da Mouraria or a similar local tasca in the Mouraria/Intendente area — hearty Portuguese home cooking (arroz de pato, grilled sardines, house wine), ~€18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The National Tile Museum is closed on Mondays mornings — check current opening hours and book the azulejo workshop in advance as spots are limited. The Mouraria walk is best experienced in the afternoon when the neighborhood's market stalls and local life are in full swing. Bring a small backpack for your handmade tile from the workshop.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Sintra, a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 40 minutes by train from Lisbon's Rossio Station. Explore the fairy-tale Palácio Nacional de Sintra (National Palace) in the town center with its distinctive twin chimneys, and hike or take a tuk-tuk up to the Moorish Castle (Castelo dos Mouros) for sweeping views over the forested hills and Atlantic coastline. The romantic landscape and royal palaces make Sintra one of Portugal's most magical day-trip destinations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lisbon by early afternoon. Spend a relaxed afternoon exploring the Príncipe Real neighborhood — one of Lisbon's most elegant and bohemian districts. Browse the Saturday antiques market (or weekday boutiques), visit the beautiful Jardim do Príncipe Real garden, and pop into the underground Reservatório da Patriarcal cistern (a hidden gem with 19th-century arched water chambers). Enjoy a coffee and people-watching at one of the charming garden-side cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lisbon's Cais do Sodré and Santos neighborhoods along the river. Visit the LX Factory — a converted 19th-century industrial complex now housing independent restaurants, bars, creative studios, and pop-up shops. Enjoy dinner and drinks in this vibrant, artsy atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at Rossio Station café before the Sintra train (~€4–6), or eat at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sintra at Casa Piriquita — a historic bakery famous for its travesseiros (almond and egg pastries) and queijadas. Or a light meal at a local restaurant in Sintra village, ~€14–20.
meals.dinner: Dinner at LX Factory — try Cantina LX for Portuguese classics or explore the market stalls for a more casual grazing dinner. Budget ~€20–30 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Trains to Sintra depart from Rossio Station every 20–30 minutes (€2.35 each way). Buy a combined ticket or use the Viva Viagem card. Sintra gets very crowded by mid-morning — aim to catch the 08:30 or 09:00 train. Wear sturdy shoes as the castle hike is steep. LX Factory is especially lively on Tuesday evenings with local creatives and a relaxed vibe.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final relaxed morning revisiting your favorite Lisbon neighborhood or checking off any remaining sights. Consider visiting the São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge) perched above Alfama for panoramic city views — it's a short walk or tuk-tuk ride from the center. Explore the castle grounds, towers, and the small archaeological museum inside. Alternatively, wander through the Feira da Ladra flea market (open Tuesdays and Saturdays) if your schedule aligns, picking up azulejo tiles, vintage postcards, and local crafts as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the elegant Avenida da Liberdade — Lisbon's grand tree-lined boulevard — window shopping at Portuguese brands like Claus Porto (artisan soaps and perfumes) and local leather goods shops. Head to the Miradouro de Santa Catarina or Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara for a final panoramic farewell view of the city. Enjoy a slow café moment with a bica and one last pastel de nata.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Lisbon — treat yourself to a slightly elevated dining experience to close the trip. Head to the Chiado or Bairro Alto area for a memorable last meal celebrating five days of Portuguese food, history, and culture.

meals.breakfast: A proper sit-down breakfast at Confeitaria Nacional on Praça da Figueira — one of Lisbon's oldest and most beautiful pastry shops (est. 1829). Try the travesseiros, queijadas, and café com leite, ~€6–8.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local tasca near Alfama or São Jorge Castle — try a simple prato do dia (dish of the day, typically €9–13 including bread, drink, and dessert).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Cervejaria Ramiro (a Lisbon seafood institution) or Taberna Sal Grosso in Intendente — fresh shellfish, grilled fish, and vinho verde. Budget €30–40 per person for a celebratory final meal. Book in advance.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is on May 20th or later, this itinerary gives you a relaxed final evening. If flying out on the evening of May 19th, adjust the afternoon to allow time for packing and airport transfer (allow at least 2.5 hours before departure). Keep the Viva Viagem metro card topped up throughout the trip — it covers metro, tram, and bus across Lisbon and saves money versus single tickets. Tip: bring home a bag of local coffee beans, a bottle of Ginjinha, and a box of pastéis de nata mix as edible souvenirs.

meals.lunch: Lunch at Solar dos Presuntos or Feitoria Restaurant & Wine Bar in Belém — a Michelin-starred restaurant with stunning Tagus River views and exceptional tasting menus rooted in Portuguese culinary heritage.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bairro do Avillez (Chef José Avillez) in Chiado — a sophisticated multi-concept space celebrating modern Portuguese gastronomy with an outstanding wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Book a private guide for the Belém monuments to skip queues and gain deeper historical insight. The Tagus riverside in Belém is particularly beautiful in the afternoon light — ideal for photography. Comfortable walking shoes are recommended.

Gain exclusive access to the convent's gilded Baroque chapel. Follow the museum visit with a hands-on azulejo painting workshop where you design and paint your own traditional tile to take home as a keepsake.

A knowledgeable local guide leads you through centuries of history, from the Reconquista to today's vibrant immigrant communities. Sample diverse street foods, visit hidden local tabernas, taste regional delicacies such as bifanas, ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur), and freshly grilled sardines at a traditional tasca.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset drink at one of Lisbon's rooftop bars — TOPO Chiado or Sky Bar at Tivoli Avenida Liberdade — with sweeping views over the city and the Tagus estuary. Then head to a refined dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel followed by a specialty coffee at a local café near the Tile Museum.
meals.lunch: Light lunch included within the Mouraria Food & History Walk — an authentic spread of local petiscos, regional wines, and traditional snacks at curated neighborhood spots.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cervejaria Ramiro — Lisbon's legendary seafood institution beloved by locals and food connoisseurs alike. Indulge in giant tiger prawns, barnacles (percebes), clams in garlic and white wine, and the famous steak sandwich finale.

day_by_day.notes: The Tile Museum is closed on Mondays — Sunday is an ideal day to visit. The azulejo workshop should be pre-booked. Mouraria is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes. Rooftop bar visit is weather-dependent — have an indoor alternative ready.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to Sintra: Hire a private driver and guide for a morning trip to the magical UNESCO World Heritage town of Sintra, just 40 minutes from Lisbon. Visit the fairytale Palácio Nacional da Pena perched dramatically on a hilltop, and explore the romantic gardens and forest paths of the Parque da Pena. Stop at the enigmatic Quinta da Regaleira with its mysterious initiation wells and esoteric architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour: Return to Lisbon in time for a curated afternoon at the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré. Rather than a standard visit, enjoy a guided premium food tour led by a local culinary expert who navigates you through the very best stalls — from Chef Alexandre Silva's Loco counter to Henrique Sá Pessoa's offerings, artisan cheeses, freshly shucked oysters, and regional pastries. Pair tastings with carefully selected Portuguese wines and craft beers.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening along the vibrant LX Factory — a repurposed 19th-century industrial complex now home to creative restaurants, art galleries, and independent boutiques. Browse the eclectic Sunday-style market atmosphere and enjoy cocktails at a stylish bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing for Sintra.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch in the Sintra hills or a refined meal at Incomum by Luis Santos in Sintra town — celebrated for contemporary Portuguese cuisine using local ingredients.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca da Esquina (Chef Vítor Sobral) — a beloved contemporary Portuguese tasca offering refined versions of traditional dishes in a warm, intimate setting in Campo de Ourique neighborhood.

day_by_day.notes: Sintra can be crowded on weekends — a private guide and driver ensures priority access and a more exclusive experience. Book Pena Palace tickets in advance. The Time Out Market food tour should be pre-arranged with a local culinary guide for a premium experience beyond the standard tourist visit.

day_by_day.morning: Begin your final morning with a leisurely private walking tour of Avenida da Liberdade — Lisbon's grand Parisian-style boulevard lined with luxury boutiques (Louis Vuitton, Cartier, Burberry) and stunning Art Deco buildings. Visit the Casa-Museu Medeiros e Almeida, a hidden gem housing one of Portugal's finest private collections of decorative arts, clocks, porcelain, and silverware in an opulent mansion setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Revisit your favorite neighborhood or explore the Príncipe Real antique market and garden. Visit the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (National Museum of Ancient Art) for a curated look at Portuguese painting, sculpture, and decorative arts spanning the 12th to 19th centuries — including the famous Panels of Saint Vincent. Allow time for last-minute luxury shopping or souvenir hunting at premium spots such as Vista Alegre (fine porcelain), Claus Porto (artisan soaps), or Napoleão wine shop.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Lisbon's most celebrated fine dining establishments — Belcanto (Chef José Avillez, two Michelin stars) in Chiado. Experience a masterful tasting menu that reimagines Portuguese culinary heritage through avant-garde techniques and the finest local ingredients, paired with an exceptional Portuguese wine flight curated by the sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the hotel — take your time and savor the full spread of local pastries, smoked fish, regional cheeses, and fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Light and elegant lunch at Pharmácia Restaurant in Chiado — set inside a beautiful old pharmacy with a charming terrace, serving creative Portuguese small plates.
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting menu dinner at Belcanto (two Michelin stars) — reserve the chef's table or private dining room for an unforgettable closing experience. Budget approximately €180–€250 per person for the full tasting menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Belcanto reservations must be made weeks in advance — book as early as possible. If departure is the following morning, arrange a private transfer to the airport and request a late checkout from the hotel to maximize your final evening. Consider purchasing a bottle of aged Vintage Port or a premium Douro red wine as a luxury memento of the trip.
